input.goal: Create a single self-contained index.html implementing an interactive full-viewport HTML5 Canvas orbital particle simulation in dark space, with a glassmorphism HUD and click-to-spawn particle bursts. Zero external dependencies, valid JavaScript.
constraints: Only one file: index.html, with inline <style> and <script>; no external URLs, fonts, images or libraries.
body/html background color #060913, margin 0, overflow hidden; canvas id="sim" is position fixed, covers the full window (100vw x 100vh).
Canvas backing size = window size * window.devicePixelRatio, with ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0); resize handler on window 'resize'.
Animation loop uses requestAnimationFrame; delta time clamped to max 0.05 s.
Central star at canvas center drawn with ctx.createRadialGradient (white core -> yellow #ffd36b -> orange -> transparent) plus a corona whose radius pulses with Math.sin of time (subtle, ~±8%).

Exactly 6 planets in window.app.planets, each object with fields: name, radius (orbital radius px), speed (rad/s), size, color, angle, trail (array of past {x,y}). Orbital radii distinct (e.g. 70,110,155,205,260,320 scaled down by Math.min(1, minDimension/720)), speeds distinct (inner faster), colors distinct.
At least 4 moons total in window.app.moons, each with fields: parent (planet index), radius, speed, size, color, angle; moons orbit their parent planet.
Orbital trails: each planet stores last ~60 positions and draws them as a fading polyline (alpha decreasing toward the oldest point). When trails are OFF, trails are not drawn and are cleared.
Background starfield: window.app.stars array with at least 200 stars, each with x,y,r,phase,twinkleSpeed; alpha = 0.3+0.7*abs(sin(time*twinkleSpeed+phase)); stars regenerated on resize.

HUD: a div id="hud" fixed top-left with glassmorphism: background rgba(255,255,255,0.08), backdrop-filter: blur(12px) (plus -webkit-backdrop-filter), border 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.18), border-radius 14px, padding 14px, color #e6ecff, font-family system-ui, sans-serif.
HUD button id="playBtn": text 'Pause' while running, 'Play' while paused; toggles window.app.paused.
HUD button id="trailsBtn": text 'Trails: ON' / 'Trails: OFF'; toggles window.app.trails (default true).

HUD button id="resetBtn": text 'Reset'; sets window.app.simTime=0, resets planet/moon angles to initial values, clears trails and all burst particles, sets speed to 1.0 and slider value to 1.0, unpauses.

Speed slider exactly: <input type="range" id="speed" min="0.2" max="3.0" step="0.1" value="1.0">; on 'input' sets window.app.speed=parseFloat(value) and updates span id="speedVal" text to speed.toFixed(1)+'x' (initially '1.0x').

HUD readouts: span id="fps" (integer FPS, smoothed, updated ~every 0.5 s), span id="simTime" (window.app.simTime.toFixed(1), seconds), span id="particles" (window.app.particles.length). Labels: 'FPS', 'Time (s)', 'Particles'.
window.app.simTime advances by dt*speed only when not paused; planets/moons stop moving when paused.

Clicking (mousedown/click event on canvas, not on HUD) spawns a radial burst of 60 particles at the click point into window.app.particles; each particle has x,y,vx,vy,life,maxLife,color,size; velocities spread evenly around 360° with random magnitude 60-260 px/s.

Particles: velocity damping each frame (v *= Math.pow(0.9, dt*60) or similar), life decreases, alpha = life/maxLife, drawn with additive blending (globalCompositeOperation 'lighter') and a glow (shadowBlur or radial gradient); removed when life<=0. Particles keep updating even when paused is false; when paused they freeze.
Expose window.app = { planets, moons, stars, particles, paused, trails, speed, simTime, spawnBurst(x,y), reset() } where spawnBurst adds the 60 particles and reset performs the Reset button behavior.
HUD must not overflow off-screen at 1280x800; buttons styled as glass pills with hover state.

I used Tandem to build `index.html`, a single self-contained file with no external dependencies. It has a glowing central star with a pulsing corona, 6 planets with moons and fading trails, a twinkling starfield of 200+ stars, and a frosted-glass control panel. Clicking the canvas sends out a burst of 60 glowing particles that slow down and fade.

Tandem's automated browser test passed, covering the parts that can be tested by script:
- **Content:** there are at least 5 planets with distinct orbit sizes and colors, at least 3 moons and at least 150 stars.
- **Buttons:** Play/Pause, Trails ON/OFF and Reset each did what they should; Reset also cleared the particles and set the speed back to 1.0.
- **Slider and burst:** the speed slider has the exact settings you specified, and moving it updates the readout. A click on the canvas spawned particles.
- **Sizing:** the canvas is scaled for high-resolution screens.

The visual parts (glow, trails, twinkling, how the bursts look) were checked only from a single screenshot. On that first screenshot, the "1.0x" speed readout ran past the panel's edge and "Trails: ON" wrapped onto two lines. I had Tandem fix the panel layout, and the second screenshot shows both fixed. The full test passed again after the fix.
